symbols.name: p
symbols.def: The number of measured scalar variables.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: The largest latent height.

symbols.name: V_l
symbols.def: \(V_0\) indexes the measured variables and \(V_\ell\) indexes scalar latent variables at height \(\ell\ge 1\).

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: The complete vertex set \(V:=\bigsqcup_{\ell=0}^{L}V_\ell\).

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: The edge set, with arrows oriented from higher to lower layers.

symbols.name: Pa
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(v):=\{u\in V:(u,v)\in E\}\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: \(X:=(X_v:v\in V_0)\) is the measured layer.

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: The joint observational law generated by a scalar structural equation model on \(G\).

symbols.name: P_X
symbols.def: The marginal law of \(X\) under \(P\).

symbols.name: f
symbols.def: For disjoint \(A,B\subseteq V_0\), \(\mathfrak F_{A,B}(P_X)\) is the set of all continuously differentiable maps on an open neighborhood \(\mathcal U_A\) of \(\operatorname{supp}(P_{X_A})\) satisfying \(g(X_A)=\mathbb E_{P_X}[X_B\mid X_A]\) \(P_X\)-almost surely.

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: For \(g\in\mathfrak F_{A,B}(P_X)\), \(J^g_{A,B}(x):=Dg(x)\).
symbols.role: derivatives indexed by all admissible versions

symbols.name: Q_stab
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\) is the set of disjoint \(A,B\subseteq V_0\) for which \(\mathfrak F_{A,B}(P_X)\neq\varnothing\) and the set \(\{\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x\sim P_{X_A}}\operatorname{rank}Dg(x):g\in\mathfrak F_{A,B}(P_X)\}\) is a singleton; pairs with an empty argument are included with value zero.

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: For \((A,B)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), \(R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(A,B)\) is the unique element of \(\{\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x\sim P_{X_A}}\operatorname{rank}Dg(x):g\in\mathfrak F_{A,B}(P_X)\}\); it is zero if either argument is empty.

symbols.name: M_PNHZ
symbols.def: The unchanged scalar layered-DAG class of Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang equipped with its observed law.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: \(B_h:=\{v\in V_\ell:\operatorname{Pa}_G(v)=\{h\}\}\), the pure-child block of \(h\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: \(D_0(v):=\{v\}\) and \(D_{\ell+1}(h):=\bigcup_{v\in B_h}D_\ell(v)\); for \(A\subseteq V_\ell\), \(D_\ell(A):=\bigcup_{v\in A}D_\ell(v)\).

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: \(\rho_\ell(A,B):=R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(D_\ell(A),D_\ell(B))\) whenever the measured pair belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The next-layer vertices represented by the recovered nontrivial pure blocks at a RankPeel iteration.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: For each \(h\in H\), \(s_h\) is the least canonically labeled member of \(B_h\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: A current nonparentless vertex outside all recovered pure blocks.

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: A candidate parent set for \(c\).

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T_C(c):=V_\ell\setminus(S_C\cup\{c\})\).

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: \(N_c(C):=\mathbf 1\{\rho_\ell(S_C,T_C(c))=\rho_\ell(S_C\cup\{c\},T_C(c))\}\).

symbols.name: RankPeel
symbols.def: The canonically ordered partial population procedure defined in \(\texttt{def:rankpeel}\); it returns \(\bot\) if a requested measured pair is outside \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\).

symbols.name: G_hat
symbols.def: \(\widehat G\) is the graph returned by a complete run of \(\operatorname{RankPeel}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X})\).

symbols.name: Transcript
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T\) records the canonical layer labels, surrogate masks, every version-stable queried pair, every returned rank, every comparison, and the final adjacency matrix of a complete RankPeel run.

symbols.name: Verify
symbols.def: The verifier replays a complete RankPeel run and re-asks exactly the version-stable rank queries recorded in \(\mathcal T\).

symbols.name: theta_G
symbols.def: \(\theta_G:=[G]\) modulo independent permutations of latent labels within each layer.

assumptions.condition: Every variable indexed by \(V\) is real-valued.

standard.name: Scalar-variable condition in the published latent-hierarchy class

assumptions.condition: For every \((u,v)\in E\), there is an \(\ell<L\) such that \(u\in V_{\ell+1}\) and \(v\in V_\ell\).
For each latent \(h\), all measured descendants of \(h\) have the same directed-path length from \(h\).
The law \(P\) obeys the directed global Markov property for \(G\).
The generalized Jacobian-rank-faithfulness Condition 2 of Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang holds for the continuously differentiable conditional-mean maps on the domains specified in that condition.

For every measured set \(A\subseteq V_0\) and latent set \(Z\subseteq V\setminus V_0\), there is a continuously differentiable \(g_{A,Z}:\mathbb R^{|A|}\to\mathbb R^{|Z|}\) such that \(P(Z\in\cdot\mid X_A=x)=P(Z\in\cdot\mid g_{A,Z}(x))\).

definitions.name: Version-invariant observed rank functional
definitions.construction: For disjoint measured \(A,B\subseteq V_0\), form \(\mathfrak F_{A,B}(P_X):=\{g\in C^1(\mathcal U_A;\mathbb R^{|B|}):\mathcal U_A\supseteq\operatorname{supp}(P_{X_A})\text{ is open and }g(X_A)=\mathbb E_{P_X}[X_B\mid X_A]\ P_X\text{-almost surely}\}\). Put \((A,B)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\) exactly when the set \(\{\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x\sim P_{X_A}}\operatorname{rank}Dg(x):g\in\mathfrak F_{A,B}(P_X)\}\) is a singleton, and define \(R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(A,B)\) as that unique integer. Empty arguments have value zero. Both the domain and value depend only on the observed law.

definitions.name: Retained pure-surrogate recursion
definitions.construction: Set \(D_0(v):=\{v\}\). After recovering \(B_h\subseteq V_\ell\), set \(D_{\ell+1}(h):=\bigcup_{v\in B_h}D_\ell(v)\) and \(D_\ell(A):=\bigcup_{v\in A}D_\ell(v)\).

definitions.name: Pairwise pure-block relation
definitions.construction: For distinct current vertices with nonempty parent sets whose measured pair query belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), \(u\sim_\ell v\) exactly when \(\rho_\ell(\{u,v\},V_\ell\setminus\{u,v\})\le 1\).

definitions.name: Representative-neutrality predicate
definitions.construction: For \(C\subseteq H\), set \(S_C:=\{s_h:h\in C\}\) and \(T_C(c):=V_\ell\setminus(S_C\cup\{c\})\). When both measured endpoint pairs belong to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), set \(N_c(C):=\mathbf 1\{\rho_\ell(S_C,T_C(c))=\rho_\ell(S_C\cup\{c\},T_C(c))\}\).

definitions.name: Version-stability and topological bottleneck audit handle
definitions.construction: For each adaptive measured endpoint pair, first compare all \(C^1\) representatives in \(\mathfrak F_{A,B}(P_X)\) by local support geometry and Whitney-extension uniqueness to determine membership in \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\). For a separator \(Z\), then start from the regular-conditional factorization of a representative through the published \(|Z|\)-dimensional sufficient map. If an \(r\times r\) minor is nonzero, restrict to an \(r\)-dimensional affine slice on which the inverse-function theorem makes a coordinate projection locally injective; because the conditional mean is constant on sufficient-map fibers, use invariance of dimension to rule out \(r>|Z|\), while auditing almost-everywhere versions.

definitions.name: Deterministic RankPeel
definitions.construction: Initialize the current layer as \(V_0\) with \(D_0(v)=\{v\}\). Before every requested lifted query, test whether its measured endpoint pair belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\); return \(\bot\) at the first unstable pair. Otherwise, at layer \(\ell\), query \(\rho_\ell(\{v\},V_\ell\setminus\{v\})\) for every current vertex and mark its zero-rank vertices as parentless; query \(\rho_\ell(\{u,v\},V_\ell\setminus\{u,v\})\) for each unordered pair of remaining vertices and take the nontrivial connected components under \(\sim_\ell\) as blocks \(B_h\); choose the least labeled \(s_h\in B_h\); for each remaining nonpure \(c\), start with \(C=H\) and process each \(h\in H\) once, deleting \(h\) exactly when \(N_c(C\setminus\{h\})=1\); record the edges from the final \(C\) to \(c\), set \(D_{\ell+1}(h)=\bigcup_{v\in B_h}D_\ell(v)\), and recurse on \(H\). A complete run returns the accumulated graph and transcript.

definitions.name: Oracle-relative replay certificate
definitions.construction: For a complete run, \(\mathcal T\) stores every canonical state, measured query mask, version-stability decision, oracle answer, comparison tag, surrogate union, and output edge. \(\operatorname{Verify}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X},\mathcal T,\widehat G)\) deterministically replays the transitions and re-asks only the recorded queries.

statements.statement: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be open, let \(a:U\to\mathbb R^q\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(b:U\to\mathbb R^k\) be continuous. If \(b(x)=b(x')\) implies \(a(x)=a(x')\), then \(\operatorname{rank}Da(x)\le k\) for every \(x\in U\).
statements.justification: This lemma removes the unjustified differentiation of the induced map while preserving the published hypotheses.
statements.gap: Prashant et al.'s Appendix applies a chain rule to an induced map whose differentiability is not stated.
statements.consumer: The restricted separator upper bound uses this lemma for every population query issued by RankPeel.

statements.statement: For every \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\), consider a measured endpoint pair \((D_\ell(A),D_\ell(B))\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\) issued by a complete RankPeel run as a singleton, pair, baseline-neutrality, or augmented-neutrality query. If a latent set \(Z\subseteq V\setminus V_0\) \(d\)-separates those endpoints in \(G\), then \(R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(D_\ell(A),D_\ell(B))\le\min\{|D_\ell(A)|,|D_\ell(B)|,|Z|\}\).
statements.justification: This is the query-specific one-way analytic implication for the law-invariant oracle and avoids a blanket rank-equals-minimum-separator identity.
statements.gap: The published argument does not establish representative stability or justify its differentiation step under Conditions 1--3 exactly as stated.
statements.consumer: Every upper half of a version-stable parentless, pure-block, or neutrality decision uses this bound.

statements.statement: For every \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\) and every \((A,B)\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), if there are \(t\) pairwise vertex-disjoint collider-free paths connecting distinct endpoints in disjoint measured sets \(A,B\subseteq V_0\), then \(R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(A,B)\ge t\).
statements.justification: Private paths give query-specific lower ranks without invoking a false global separator identity.
statements.gap: Trek separation proves the analogous generic noncancellation for linear Gaussian covariance ranks, while the anchor uses a broad generalized-faithfulness assertion rather than this explicit witness move.
statements.consumer: The lower bound distinguishes different parent sets in pair tests and supplies the exact one-rank neutrality increment.

statements.statement: At every level \(\ell\), distinct sets \(D_\ell(v)\) are disjoint retained pure-descendant trees. In the ancestral graph of retained endpoints: \(V_\ell\)-roots separate their own surrogate trees from other retained trees; any \(C\subseteq V_{\ell+1}\) containing all parents of source roots separates those source surrogate trees from the other retained trees; and each current-layer private fork lifts to a collider-free measured path, with vertex-disjoint forks lifting to vertex-disjoint paths.
statements.justification: The lemma is the recursive invariant that keeps every query observable after latent contraction.
statements.gap: Published surrogate statements are broader or are proved in linear latent-cover models; discarded mixed descendants make a blanket separation statement false here.
statements.consumer: RankPeel can peel all layers without assuming that an unobserved contracted law inherits generalized faithfulness.

statements.statement: For every current \(v\in V_\ell\) whose singleton measured endpoint pair belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), \(\rho_\ell(\{v\},V_\ell\setminus\{v\})=0\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(v)=\varnothing\).
statements.justification: Roots at different heights must be removed before pair clustering to prevent false rank-one links.
statements.gap: The anchor supplies the ingredients for recursive root detection inside its exhaustive identification construction; the distinct claim here is the exact singleton decision used by the deterministic pairwise RankPeel protocol.
statements.consumer: The proposition prevents isolated or parentless vertices from contaminating pure-block components.

statements.statement: For distinct current vertices \(u,v\in V_\ell\) with nonempty parent sets whose pair-query measured endpoints belong to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), \(\rho_\ell(\{u,v\},V_\ell\setminus\{u,v\})\le1\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(u)=\operatorname{Pa}_G(v)=\{h\}\) for some \(h\in V_{\ell+1}\). Consequently, on a complete run the nontrivial connected components of \(\sim_\ell\) are exactly the pure blocks \(B_h\).
statements.justification: A pairwise criterion replaces the anchor's all-subsets pure-child search.
statements.gap: Prashant et al.'s pure-child lemma quantifies over all subsets and does not provide this pairwise equivalence or its recursive observed-surrogate form.
statements.consumer: Every latent parent and its full pure-child block becomes recoverable with at most one query per current pair.

statements.statement: Let \(H=V_{\ell+1}\), choose any \(s_h\in B_h\), let \(c\in V_\ell\) be nonparentless and outside every pure block, and take \(C\subseteq H\) with \(k=|C|\). If the baseline and augmented measured endpoint pairs belong to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), then \(\rho_\ell(S_C,T_C(c))=k\) and \(\rho_\ell(S_C\cup\{c\},T_C(c))=k\) when \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(c)\subseteq C\), whereas the augmented rank is \(k+1\) otherwise. Hence \(N_c(C)=1\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Pa}_G(c)\subseteq C\), independently of representative choices.
statements.justification: The exact \(k\)-versus-\(k+1\) increment turns mixed-child parent recovery into monotone deletion.
statements.gap: The anchor tests parent subsets and all representative selections; it does not state one-representative neutrality, representative invariance, or deletion-order independence.
statements.consumer: One test per candidate parent recovers arbitrary-indegree mixed-child parent sets.

statements.statement: Theorem 1 (Law-invariant RankPeel reconstruction on complete runs). For every \((G,P)\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\), if every measured endpoint pair adaptively requested by \(\operatorname{RankPeel}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X})\) belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), then RankPeel terminates with \(\widehat G\) satisfying \([\widehat G]=\theta_G\). It recovers the same full binary adjacency matrix identified by Theorem 3 of Prashant et al., with only within-layer latent-label permutations, but replaces their exhaustive subset construction by deterministic pairwise pure-block tests and representative-neutrality deletion over measured pure-descendant surrogates.
statements.justification: The theorem converts same-class identification into a deterministic pairwise and deletion protocol whenever the observed law fixes every requested derivative rank.
statements.gap: Prashant et al. already identify the full binary adjacency matrix and already use measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates, but their exhaustive subset construction has no deterministic quadratic observed-query guarantee.
statements.consumer: The theorem gives latent-hierarchy researchers a canonical complete-run population benchmark with an explicit list of observed-law queries.

statements.statement: Theorem 2 (Quadratic oracle complexity). If \(|V_0|=p\), RankPeel returns either \(\bot\) or a graph after at most \(p^2+p\) membership-and-rank calls to the law-invariant oracle, \(O(p^3)\) elementary bookkeeping, \(O(p^2)\) graph storage, and at most \(1+\lfloor\log_2 p\rfloor\) nonempty iterations. On the complete-run domain of Theorem 1, this is a strict query-complexity tightening of the exhaustive subset construction in Prashant et al. for the same identified adjacency target.
statements.justification: The explicit budget isolates the algorithmic gain over exhaustive subset enumeration without claiming a stronger identified graph.
statements.gap: The anchor identifies the same adjacency matrix but does not give a polynomial observed-query bound for its subset construction.
statements.consumer: The bound fixes the complete family of population decisions that subsequent statistical calibration must cover simultaneously.

statements.statement: Corollary 1 (Replay record). Every complete RankPeel run emits a transcript \(\mathcal T\) of \(O(p^3+p^2\log p)\) bits for which \(\operatorname{Verify}(P_X,R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X},\mathcal T,\widehat G)=1\). Replaying it uses at most \(p^2+p\) law-invariant oracle calls and \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping; under Theorem 1 its recorded graph represents \(\theta_G\).
statements.justification: The corollary records the decisions supporting a complete run without elevating deterministic replay into a separate identification theorem.
statements.gap: The anchor does not package its exhaustive construction as a compact canonical query transcript.
statements.consumer: An implementation can reproduce every population decision made by the deterministic protocol.

statements.statement: For a linear Gaussian member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{PNHZ}}\) with nonsingular measured covariance, the conditional mean has a unique \(P_{X_A}\)-essential derivative, \(J_{A,B}=\operatorname{Cov}(X_B,X_A)\operatorname{Cov}(X_A,X_A)^{-1}\), so every RankPeel pair lies in \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\) and its law-invariant query rank equals the corresponding cross-covariance rank. The restricted separator upper bounds and private-path lower bounds therefore reduce to Gaussian trek separation and generic noncancellation.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check and locates the nonlinear theorem relative to known linear rank geometry.
statements.gap: The linear literature does not supply the nonlinear analytic factorization or this same-class deterministic certificate.
statements.consumer: Implementations can validate exact RankPeel transcripts on rational linear Gaussian SEMs before estimating nonlinear Jacobians.

statements.statement: Open-ended Question 1. Do the exact Conditions 1--3 of Prashant et al. imply that every measured endpoint pair adaptively requested by RankPeel belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\) and that every restricted surrogate separator cut obeys \(R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}(A,B)\le |Z|\)? If not, characterize the weakest observable support and conditional-version regularity that gives both properties, and exhibit a legal smooth scalar SEM immediately below that boundary.
statements.justification: This question separates the unresolved version-stability and separator-factorization obligations from the combinatorial reconstruction theorem.
statements.gap: The anchor's pointwise derivative notation does not show that essential-supremum rank is invariant across conditional-mean versions, and its chain-rule proof does not resolve the issue.
statements.consumer: A solution determines whether complete law-invariant RankPeel recovery holds on the entire published class or only on an explicitly characterized support-regular subclass.

sampling_model.design: Population observational identification; there is no intervention or randomization design.
sampling_model.units: One scalar random vector indexed by the finite layered vertex set, with only \(X\) observed.
sampling_model.treatment: None; the target is the causal structure rather than a treatment effect.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None in the core theorem. The partial functional \(R^{\mathrm{law}}_{P_X}\) is determined by the observed law on \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), and oracle evaluation cost is excluded from query complexity.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The full binary adjacency matrix is identifiable up to permutation of latent variables, using measured pure descendants as recursive surrogates in an exhaustive subset construction.
The proposed algorithm can find the correct Markov equivalence class of the whole graph asymptotically under proper restrictions.
The estimated variable and the true variable are equivalent up to an invertible transformation.
Trek separation gives a complete characterization of when covariance submatrices drop rank and their generic lower rank.

tldr: Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang already identify the full binary adjacency matrix of their nonlinear latent hierarchy and already reuse measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates. The contribution is a deterministic RankPeel protocol that replaces their exhaustive subset construction by pairwise pure-block tests and representative-neutrality deletion, giving at most \(p^2+p\) observed queries and \(O(p^3)\) bookkeeping on complete runs. To keep those queries invariant under the observed law, the rank functional is defined only where all continuously differentiable conditional-mean representatives have the same essential-supremum derivative rank; RankPeel returns \(\bot\) otherwise. Exact recovery on complete runs, the restricted separator and private-path lemmas, and the quadratic bound are theorem targets. Whether the unchanged published Conditions 1--3 guarantee version stability and hence completeness for every class member is the explicit analytic open question; replay is only a corollary.

project_justification.gap: The closest nonlinear result already identifies the complete binary adjacency matrix and already uses measured pure descendants as recursive surrogates, but its construction exhaustively searches subset families and gives no explicit polynomial bound on observed rank queries. Its pointwise conditional-mean derivative notation also does not establish invariance across regular-conditional versions.
project_justification.niche: The same published model class admits a potentially sharper algorithmic formulation: pairwise block discovery and monotone parent deletion can reduce the number of observed-law rank decisions, provided every adaptive derivative-rank query is version-stable.
project_justification.fill: RankPeel supplies the deterministic pairwise and deletion protocol, a \(p^2+p\) complete-run query bound, and a replay corollary. A law-invariant stability domain prevents arbitrary pointwise versions from entering the oracle, while the exact Conditions 1--3 completeness obligation remains an open theorem-level boundary rather than a new assumption.

related_work: Prashant, Ng, Zhang, and Huang identify the full binary adjacency matrix up to latent permutation and use measured pure descendants as higher-layer surrogates; Theorem 2 tightens only the query construction, replacing their exhaustive subset search by a deterministic pairwise and deletion protocol with an explicit quadratic observed-query bound on version-stable complete runs. Huang, Low, Xie, Glymour, and Zhang inform the same pure-descendant surrogate motif in a linear IL\(^{2}\)H model, but their covariance-rank assumptions and Markov-equivalence target differ. Kong, Huang, Xie, Xing, Chi, and Zhang inform the layerwise nonlinear setting but identify latent representations through invertible transformations rather than an observed-law derivative-rank protocol. Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma inform the separation of graph-forced upper bounds from generic path-based lower bounds in linear Gaussian models. Chen and Fang and Cattaneo, Feng, and Shigida address the distinct nonregular rank-testing and uniform derivative-inference problems outside this population core.
technical_internal_limitation: The prescribed enumeration covered all \(676\) stated three-level graphs and all \(58{,}188\) proposed level-zero and retained-surrogate cuts, but finite enumeration does not prove the recursive graphical lemma. More importantly, the unchanged published Conditions 1--3 provide differentiable conditional-mean versions but do not by themselves identify a pointwise derivative rank across versions on arbitrary observed supports. The core therefore uses the observed-law domain \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{stab}}(P_X)\), makes exact reconstruction conditional on a complete run, and leaves full-class version stability plus the restricted separator upper bound as the analytic obligation. No blanket separator-equals-rank identity, saturated-rank condition, or faithfulness inheritance after latent contraction is assumed.
honest_scope: The target remains population recovery of the full binary adjacency matrix on the unchanged Prashant--Ng--Zhang--Huang class, not a stronger identified graph than the anchor provides. The settled proposal-level advance sought is algorithmic: deterministic pairwise and deletion queries, a quadratic complete-run bound, and a replay corollary. Exact recovery is stated only when every adaptive pair lies in the observed-law version-stability domain. Whether the published Conditions 1--3 force that completeness and the restricted separator upper bound is open. The proposal does not cover polynomial-time evaluation of the oracle, nonparametric Jacobian estimation, finite-sample recovery, or image-data consistency. In the nonsingular linear Gaussian special case, version stability holds and query ranks reduce to covariance-rank geometry.

seed_details.rebuttal: The published hypotheses do not state the differentiability needed for that chain rule; a proof under the exact hypotheses is a foundational repair used by every subsequent rank-identification claim.

seed_details.title: Oracle-query lower bound for latent-hierarchy reconstruction
seed_details.opened_evidence: The anchor gives no oracle decision-tree complexity, leaving open whether quadratic queries are intrinsic or merely sufficient.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct a relatively open faithful family whose mixed-child parent matrices encode many distinguishable graphs while each admissible rank query has a controlled answer alphabet.
seed_details.destination_search: No inspected latent-hierarchy paper proves a rank-oracle lower bound for complete adjacency recovery.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Characterize the minimax deterministic query complexity of exact reconstruction and seek an \(\Omega(p^2/\log p)\) or sharper lower bound matched by RankPeel up to logarithms.
seed_details.open_content: Build an adversarial faithful graph family for which adaptive block queries cannot reveal many parent bits simultaneously.
seed_details.cynical_objection: A counting argument makes the lower bound routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: Rank answers take multiple integer values and large block queries can aggregate many edges, so the needed adversarial indistinguishability family is not delivered by graph counting alone.

seed_details.title: Query-restricted conditional-sufficiency frontier
seed_details.anchor_location: Condition 3(ii), proof of Theorem 1, and Conclusion
seed_details.opened_evidence: The conclusion explicitly identifies relaxation of the differentiability and conditional-sufficiency condition as future work, while the reconstruction proof uses only a restricted family of rank upper bounds.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the global density factorization \(p(z\mid x)=p(z\mid g(x))\) by a query-indexed factorization of only the relevant conditional-mean maps through continuous \(|Z|\)-dimensional bottlenecks.
seed_details.destination_search: Kong et al. use invertible recovery of latent variables and disturbances, which is a different and stronger route; no inspected paper characterizes the weakest operator condition for these restricted Jacobian queries.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Give necessary and sufficient observable-operator conditions for all RankPeel query ranks, with a counterexample immediately outside the condition.
seed_details.open_content: Prove necessity without building the answer into a named surrogate map and determine whether a common bottleneck is required across adaptive queries.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This merely renames Condition 3 on a smaller query set.
seed_details.rebuttal: An acceptable result must give both directions and a boundary counterexample, not assume the queried rank inequalities or restate the published sufficient statistic.

seed_details.title: Generic nonlinear Jacobian-rank faithfulness
seed_details.anchor_location: Proposition 1 and Appendix proof of Proposition 1
seed_details.opened_evidence: The proposition invokes independently continuously drawn matrix entries, whereas Jacobian factors generated by one structural model are functionally dependent and the unrestricted function class has no canonical Lebesgue measure.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Specify a finite-dimensional analytic SEM parameterization and witness one nonzero queried minor per graphically unentailed constraint before applying analytic zero-set arguments.
seed_details.destination_search: Sullivant, Talaska, and Draisma obtain genericity from nonzero trek determinant polynomials in linear Gaussian models; no inspected nonlinear hierarchy paper supplies the analogous parameterized minor argument.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Show that generalized rank faithfulness for the finite RankPeel query family holds outside a proper analytic subset of a specified nonlinear SEM parameter space, or exhibit an open family of structural cancellations.
seed_details.open_content: Choose a parameterization broad enough to be substantively nonlinear while retaining a rigorous genericity measure and dependent Jacobian factors.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Generic full rank follows immediately because rank-deficient matrices have Lebesgue measure zero.
seed_details.rebuttal: That argument fails for structurally dependent matrix factors; the missing contribution is to prove the relevant determinant is not identically zero on the SEM parameter image.

seed_details.title: Complete inconsistency certificates for rank transcripts
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 3 and the released algorithmic formulation
seed_details.opened_evidence: The anchor returns a graph under its model assumptions but does not characterize which observed rank transcripts are incompatible with every graph in the class.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Turn pairwise clique failures, dimension violations, and mutually inconsistent neutrality answers into a finite obstruction system indexed by the same observed queries.
seed_details.destination_search: The inspected recovery results provide correctness under assumptions, not completeness of an observed-rank rejection certificate for this nonlinear class.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Characterize a polynomially checkable family of transcript obstructions that is sound, and determine whether it is complete for membership in the RankPeel rank-pattern image.
seed_details.open_content: Completeness may require global constraints beyond the local peeling transcript.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The certificate is just a log of the algorithm and says nothing about assumption failure.
seed_details.rebuttal: The seed is retained only in its stronger obstruction-completeness form; a replay log alone is assigned to the main reconstruction seed as a corollary.

seed_details.title: Asynchronous peeling without equal measured-descendant depth
seed_details.opened_evidence: Equal measured-descendant path length creates the layer alignment used by recursion but is not characterized as necessary.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the common active layer by a frontier of pure-surrogate trees of unequal depths and characterize which frontier updates preserve separator cuts.
seed_details.destination_search: The inspected nonlinear hierarchy and linear rank-recovery papers impose their own layer or latent-cover restrictions and do not give an exact frontier for unequal-depth observed leaves under conditional-mean Jacobian ranks.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Characterize when an asynchronous RankPeel frontier identifies the full DAG without the equal-depth condition, with a pair of observationally equivalent graphs at the boundary.
seed_details.open_content: Find a graph-invariant observable rule for deciding which surrogate blocks may be advanced without exposing discarded mixed descendants.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Unequal depth is a routine bookkeeping extension.
seed_details.rebuttal: The current surrogate-separation proof relies on a common attachment level; advancing one branch can change both the endpoint class and the valid cut, so necessity and a boundary witness are substantive.

seed_details.title: Observed-parent nonlinear hierarchy recovery
seed_details.anchor_location: Conclusion discussion of measured variables with children
seed_details.opened_evidence: The conclusion excludes structures in which measured variables have children and names their inclusion as future work.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Modify parentless detection because rank zero against the observed complement no longer distinguishes a measured root from a measured parent whose effects propagate downward.
seed_details.destination_search: Dong et al. treat causally related hidden variables in a linear partially observed network, but the inspected literature contains no nonlinear conditional-mean-Jacobian analogue with certified complete recovery.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Recover the partially observed nonlinear DAG up to its unavoidable equivalence class using an augmented family of conditional-mean Jacobian queries.
seed_details.open_content: Characterize the exact equivalence class once observed-to-observed and observed-to-latent arrows are admitted.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Dong et al. already allow measured variables inside the causal network.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their linear rank setting and target differ; the seed survives only if it derives a nonlinear observed functional and an exact equivalence characterization rather than translating their algorithm.

seed_details.title: Finite-sample simultaneous RankPeel certification
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1, the differentiable population criterion, and experimental implementation
seed_details.opened_evidence: The population theory does not estimate the essential-supremum ranks along an adaptively selected transcript.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct simultaneous confidence bands for conditional-mean derivatives before composing them with nonregular trailing-singular-value rank decisions over the adaptive query tree.
seed_details.destination_search: Chen and Fang treat composite finite-matrix rank nulls, while Cattaneo, Feng, and Shigida treat uniform nonparametric regression functionals; no inspected result composes both pieces for adaptive latent-graph reconstruction.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Give a sample-size and singular-value-margin condition under which every adaptive rank decision, the replay transcript, and the full graph are jointly correct with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).
seed_details.open_content: Control the essential supremum and selection over a query family whose membership depends on earlier noisy rank outcomes.
seed_details.cynical_objection: A union bound over at most \(p^2+p\) tests makes this immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform derivative estimation and composite-rank calibration at lower-rank boundary points are both nonregular; a union bound applies only after simultaneous valid query-level confidence events are derived.

literature_map.inspected_parts: Introduction, Conditions 1--3, Theorems 1--3, proofs in Appendix A, and Conclusion.
literature_map.settled: The paper identifies the full binary adjacency matrix up to latent permutation and uses measured pure descendants as recursive surrogates.
literature_map.boundary: Its construction searches subsets and gives no polynomial observed-query bound; its conditional-mean derivative rank is not shown invariant across pointwise versions under arbitrary observed supports.

literature_map.inspected_parts: Introduction, Theorems 1--3, causal-cluster search, edge refinement, and consistency theorem.
literature_map.settled: Covariance-rank tests recover a Markov equivalence class for the paper's linear IL\(^{2}\)H model through latent-cover search and refinement.
literature_map.boundary: The model, rank functional, structural restrictions, and returned graph object differ, and the search still ranges over subsets.

literature_map.inspected_parts: Introduction, basis-model theorem, local and global identification sections, and Conclusion.
literature_map.settled: Latent variables and hierarchical structure are identified by invertible representation recovery under information-conservation, span, and connectivity conditions.
literature_map.boundary: This route estimates latent representations and assumes invertible recovery of latent variables and disturbances; it does not give the observed rank-oracle protocol.

literature_map.thread: Graphical rank factorization and generic lower bounds
literature_map.inspected_parts: Introduction, directed trek-separation theorem, determinant-path expansion, and genericity discussion.
literature_map.settled: For linear Gaussian DAGs, trek separation characterizes covariance-submatrix rank constraints, with generic equality from nonzero determinant polynomials.
literature_map.boundary: Finite polynomial factorizations do not justify differentiating the nonlinear conditional-distribution factorization, but the separation of upper and lower arguments motivates the query-specific proof architecture.

literature_map.inspected_parts: Introduction, positivity theorem for acyclic digraphs, and cancellation-free subdeterminant formula.
literature_map.settled: Nonzero Gaussian graphical-model subdeterminants admit cancellation-free expansions over trek systems.
literature_map.boundary: The finite polynomial representation supplies a rigorous genericity template, but nonlinear conditional-mean Jacobians generated by one SEM do not inherit that polynomial structure.

literature_map.inspected_parts: Theorem statements and method descriptions identified in the literature substrate.
literature_map.settled: Composite matrix-rank nulls require nonregular calibration, and uniform nonparametric regression transformations admit strong approximations under their sampling conditions.
literature_map.boundary: Neither paper supplies population exact reconstruction or the composition needed for an adaptive essential-supremum Jacobian transcript.
